overview: Black meets 2.Nc3 with ...c5, challenging d4 at once. White can play 3.d5 for a Benoni-style game, 3.dxc5 or 3.e4, or 3.Nf3 with a transposition. Black aims for active piece play, often a Benoni or Sicilian-like structure, while White uses the extra move compared to the Chigorin to take space. I am unsure of the details of this branch.

white_ideas.idea: Gain space with d5 or e4 and build a centre.
Develop Nf3, e3 and Bd3 and keep the position flexible.

black_ideas.idea: Challenge d4 with ...c5 and ...cxd4, using the half-open c-file.
Develop with ...g6, ...Bg7 and a Benoni or Sicilian-like set-up.

typical_structures.structure: Benoni-like or Sicilian-like pawn asymmetry after d5 or dxc5.

character.notes: An unusual move order with several transpositions; not especially forcing.

structure.notes: Centre tension after ...c5, not yet resolved.

approach.notes: Rare; chosen mainly to avoid mainstream theory.

sublines_that_differ.name: Von Beivorseen
sublines_that_differ.how: White grabs the pawn and the game has a more open, tactical flavour.

gambit.reason: No sacrifice in the main line.

plans.reason: Black attacks the centre rather than occupying it.
